description: New marketplace app installs can expose Drive/Gmail data; tracks installs and OAuth scopes. Searches `index=gws` with sourcetype `gws:token` for UC-11.2.12, aggregating `values` by `app_name` over `the scheduled window`. Alerts when grouped results cross configured threshold in the saved search. Gives Operations operators a repeatable signal for 'Workspace Marketplace App Review' without manual log review.
value: Early 'Workspace Marketplace App Review' detection reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by giving Operations operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `gws`** — Planned work for 'Workspace Marketplace App Review' shifts `values` over `span=1h` while `app_name` remains in-scope for UC-11.2.12. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `values` on `gws:token`** — Scheduled automation elevates `actor.email` without crossing configured threshold. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `app_name`** — Health checks in `gws` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `gws:token`** — First 48h baseline for `app_name` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `app_name`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: `Splunk_TA_GoogleWorkspace`.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: Token audit (`authorize`), admin audit (`ADD_APPLICATION`, `INSTALL_MARKETPLACE_APP`).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Maintain allowlist of approved apps. Alert on new apps with sensitive scopes. Quarterly access review with app owners.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=gws sourcetype="gws:token" event_name="authorize"
| stats values(scope) as scopes by app_name, actor.email
| mvexpand scopes limit=500
| search scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive" OR scopes="*gmail*"
| sort app_name
```

Understanding this SPL

**Workspace Marketplace App Review** — New marketplace app installs can expose Drive/Gmail data; tracks installs and OAuth scopes.

Documented **Data sources**: Token audit (`authorize`), admin audit (`ADD_APPLICATION`, `INSTALL_MARKETPLACE_APP`). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): `Splunk_TA_GoogleWorkspace`. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: gws; **sourcetype**: gws:token. If that sourcetype is not mentioned in Data sources, double-check parsing or update the documentation to match the feed you actually ingest.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=gws, sourcetype="gws:token". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by app_name, actor.email** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• Expands multivalue fields with `mvexpand` — use `limit=` to cap row explosion.
• Applies an explicit `search` filter to narrow the current result set.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.


Step 3 — Validate
Compare with Google Admin console audit and Google Workspace reports for the same org unit and time window.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Table (high-risk grants), Bar chart (apps by user count), Pie chart (scope categories).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk_TA_GoogleWorkspace` — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=gws:token into gws. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`actor.email, app_name`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
